subject: Request: subprocessor residency & proof-set for ProcureCo due diligence
messages:
From: Alice Dunn <alice.dunn@procureco.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: ProcureCo Procurement <procurement@procureco.com>
Date: 2025-10-14T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: ProcureCo diligence: subprocessor residency & proof-set request

Hi Monica,

Hope you’re well. As part of ProcureCo’s vendor intake we need a compact proof-set from Redwood covering: a current subprocessor roster with geographic residency for each provider, the KMS custody model for any encryption keys that protect customer data, and mapping to your most recent SOC 2/CAIQ/SIG deliverables.

Concretely, could you provide the following by Oct 21?
- CSV roster with columns: vendor name, service provided, country of processing, access scope, contact.
- SOC 2 attestation (redacted OK) and a CAIQ/ SIG mapping doc that ties services to evidence artifacts.
- Notes on patch cadence (CVE response SLAs) and onshore/offshore restrictions for PII.

If it helps, we can take a short call next week to walk the materials.

Thanks,
Alice Dunn
ProcureCo — Security & Procurement
[email: alice.dunn@procureco.com]

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Alice Dunn <alice.dunn@procureco.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-10-14T10:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: ProcureCo diligence: subprocessor residency & proof-set request

Alice — thanks for the clear list. Attaching a compact roster (subprocessors_20251014.csv) that includes residency and access scope; I've also attached a short SOC 2 summary (redwood_soc2_attestation_summary.pdf) that we can share with your team.

Quick notes up front:
- Residency: most production processing occurs in US (us-west-2) and EU (eu-west-1); we flag any APAC subprocessors in the CSV.
- KMS custody: for Redwood Hosted customers we use a Redwood-managed KMS in AWS (us-west-2) with strict IAM boundaries; for Private deployments we support customer-managed keys (BYOK) on request.
- Patch cadence: monthly security updates; critical CVEs pushed to infra within 72 hours after confirmation and prioritized fixes for inference runtime components.

Ben/Marissa — can you confirm the CAIQ mapping and whether we want to include the CAIQ workbook as the formal artifact? Also want to confirm whether we should provide a redacted vendor contract excerpt for the handful of subprocessors that handle sensitive telemetry.

Attachments: subprocessors_20251014.csv, redwood_soc2_attestation_summary.pdf

Best,
Monica Patel
Senior Manager, Security Partnerships
Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0132

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-10-15T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: ProcureCo diligence: subprocessor residency & proof-set request

Adding a few specifics for ProcureCo that you can forward:
- SOC 2: most recent Type II period ended 2025-06-30; full report available under NDA. Included with this reply is a 2-page public summary and our attestation date (see redwood_soc2_attestation_summary.pdf).
- CAIQ/SIG: I prepared a mapping workbook (caiaq_mapping_20251015.xlsx) that maps our runtime, control plane and telemetry artifacts to typical CAIQ questions — it'll speed review for ProcureCo.
- KMS detail: Hosted mode uses Redwood-managed AWS KMS (keys in us-west-2); customers requiring dedicated key control can use our Dedicated/Private offering or BYOK via AWS KMS or external HSM. We do not hold customer private keys for BYOK.
- Residency nuance: CDN and edge cache partner has POPs in APAC but they only cache non-PII assets (no logs or user content). Any subprocessors that process content containing PII are listed with country and contract clause in the CSV.
- CVE/patch cadence: monthly planned updates; emergency patches for critical issues are triaged 24–72 hours and we have a documented incident process.

If ProcureCo needs a redacted copy of vendor agreements for specific subprocessors, we can provide redlines on request — note that some vendors require NDAs for contract excerpts.

I’ll attach the CAIQ workbook and a short mapping PDF. Monica — happy for you to push these to Alice.

Attachments: caiaq_mapping_20251015.xlsx, redwood_soc2_attestation_summary.pdf

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Director, Third-Party Risk
Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

From: Alice Dunn <alice.dunn@procureco.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: ProcureCo Procurement <procurement@procureco.com>
Date: 2025-10-16T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: ProcureCo diligence: subprocessor residency & proof-set request

Monica / Ben — thanks, this is helpful. A couple of follow-ups: 
1) Could you export the roster with an explicit column for ‘PII processing: yes/no’ and a contact at each vendor for escalation?
2) We’ll need a confirmation line that for Hosted customers, PII is not exported outside the listed processing regions without explicit customer authorization. Can you confirm that and provide suggested DPA language?
3) Please add the CAIQ workbook link to the Drive folder and share a DocuSign-ready DPA redline (procureco-dpa-redline.docx) we can route internally.

Would you be available for a 30-minute call the week of Oct 20 to walk the materials and a proposed DPA clause? If so, send a calendar invite and we’ll accept.

Appreciate the fast turnaround — this will keep our procurement timeline on track.

Best,
Alice Dunn
ProcureCo — Security & Procurement
alice.dunn@procureco.com
